name: POST /api/leadflow/intake/webhooks/:platform - Per-provider receiver
description:
The receiver a platform posts to directly. Authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW body rather than by a bearer token — a provider has no LeadFlow session and cannot be given one, which is why requiresAuth is false here and true on the sibling /events route.

ANSWERS 200 FOR ALMOST EVERYTHING, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Providers retry on any non-2xx, so returning 4xx for a payload we have permanently refused makes them redeliver it on a schedule we do not control, indefinitely. A rejected signal is archived and answered 200.

THE ONE EXCEPTION IS A BAD SIGNATURE, which MUST be non-2xx. It is the only response that tells a sender their secret is wrong; swallowing it with 200 would leave a misconfigured integration looking healthy while nothing at all lands. Unsigned, wrongly-signed, and a platform with no configured secret are all 401 — and all three are ARCHIVED FIRST, because a refused webhook that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from one that never arrived.

AN UNCONFIGURED PLATFORM IS REFUSED, NOT WAVED THROUGH. Accepting from a platform we hold no secret for would mean anything posted to /intake/webhooks/anything lands. An unconfigured integration should be a 401 somebody notices, not an open door nobody does.

The digest is computed over the exact bytes received. Re-serialising parsed JSON reorders keys and changes whitespace, so a signature checked against the re-encoded form fails for perfectly valid payloads — intermittently, depending on the sender's key order, which is a miserable thing to diagnose. The comparison is constant-time: a plain equality check leaks through timing how many leading bytes of a guess were right.

The failure message is IDENTICAL for a wrong signature and a length mismatch, so a caller cannot use the difference to narrow their search.

testCases.name: Reject a platform with no configured secret rather than waving it through

errorCases.message: platform is required in the path
The signature did not match the payload
errorCases.when: the request is unsigned, wrongly signed, or from a platform with no configured signing secret. The message is identical for a wrong signature and a length mismatch so a caller cannot narrow their search.
